_comment: Hand-maintained rename table for stop identity. Pipeline input only — this
file is never shipped to the client. See scripts/README.md for provenance and
for how to add an entry.
Keys and values are UNPREFIXED slugs, as produced by stop_identity.stop_key
before the 'bus:'/'rail:' prefix is attached. An entry folds one spelling of a
stop onto the canonical slug for that place, so a stop Metro has renamed keeps
one continuous series instead of splitting into two, and so the ridership export
and GTFS agree on which dot a stop is. Chains are followed; cycles raise.
The bus table is empty. Checked across all five archives in data/raw/: no month
in the 2025-07..2026-06 window has both an added and a dropped key, which is the
signature a rename leaves. Thirteen bus stops have ridership and no geometry;
they are listed in src/data/stop_locations.json's `unmatched` and are kept, not
dropped. Naming them would take a map, not the data — see scripts/README.md.
The one ambiguous case — line 28's san-vicente-fairfax ->
san-vicente-orange-grove — is still left alone on purpose.
The rail table holds the GTFS-side mismatches the geometry join found (PR 2).
Every entry was confirmed against the export's per-route station sequence and
the GTFS coordinates, not against the names alone; the evidence is in
scripts/README.md. Eight fold the export's disused spelling onto the name GTFS
uses now. The two expo-crenshaw entries run the other way, because GTFS carries
*only* per-platform spellings for that interchange ('Expo / Crenshaw E-Line
Station', '... K-Line Station') and no clean one — so the export's spelling is
the canonical slug and the two platforms fold onto it, which is what
strip_rail_platform_suffix would have done had the suffix been spelled with a
space rather than a hyphen.
